sentences.text: Ontario described communicable disease surveillance as involving the collection, analysis, and distribution of laboratory and healthcare facility data on infectious diseases through a comprehensive provincial surveillance system.
Ontario established a Surveillance and Outbreak Management Section of Public Health Division to support communicable disease surveillance operations.
Ontario developed the Integrated Public Health Information System (iPHIS) for infectious disease reporting, contact tracing, and quarantine management.

Ontario recognized that comparable surveillance data are essential to estimate the size of a health problem and to determine its economic burden on society, to characterize trends, and to evaluate intervention and prevention programs.
